title: Nice 1976: Illinois Jaquet, the 'king', and Bud Johnson
summary: At the 1976 Nice festival, musicians gathered in Bud Johnson's room. Jaquet announced himself king of tenor, and the two agreed to a showdown, with Jaquet arriving drunk with a soprano.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: You know, a little rougher, you know, and Bud Johnson is rougher, but he's -- I'll tell you a story of Illinois Jaquet and Bud. We were in Nice in 1976, and we stayed at the Meridian Hotel, and every night they had a jam session all night long, and everybody congregated there. It was a beautiful year.

And after that we'd mostly go up and hang out in Bud's room, Dizzy and Illinois and myself and Jackson, Oliver Jackson, all go up to Bud's room. You know, I never drank -- I wasn't drinking but joined the rest of them and watch them drink and tell tales.
So one night we were sitting up there in this -- in Bud's room talking and everything, and a knock came on the door. And I opened the door and here, Illinois walks in, let
the king in. Let the king --

And Bud jumped up and said, 'the king of what?' He says, 'the king, the king tenor player.' Bud says, 'Look, man. Go get your horn. I'll show you who's the king.' So they're talking. So finally they made up a pact, said, 'tomorrow night we'll meet downstairs, and I'll show you the king. Bring your horn down.'

So Bud said I'm -- Bud and Illinois are going to battle it out, so I said, 'Well, I'll bring mine down too, and we'll just all have a good time.' So that next night here comes -- Bud was down, and here comes Illinois with a soprano, drunk as he could be with a soprano saxophone.
A soprano, I never heard of him play Bud with the soprano.

That's what he had, you know, because, you know, he was asking for trouble, you know, because he's going to cut Bud, and Bud is pretty rough, you know, and I was going to get in it just for the fun of it, because I'm a new tenor player, and I relish this kind of thing anyway, you know.
So Bud said, 'The king of what?' Well, that's what he calls himself, the king.
Uh-huh. Well, he had that number with Basie. But, you know, it's --
